page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Substitute t = logx
steps.why: Exactly the same substitution as the previous question — 1/x dx becomes dt once t=logx — leaving a plain cott dt to integrate.
common_mistakes: Confusing ∫cott dt with ∫tant dt — they give DIFFERENT standard results.
Forgetting the substitution converts dx/x, not just dx, into dt.
steps.memory_tip: 1/x next to any function of logx ⇒ the same t=logx substitution, every time.

steps.label: Integrate and back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: ∫cott dt = log|sint| + c is a standard result, and substituting t=logx back in returns the answer in terms of x.
common_mistakes: Writing log|cos(logx)| instead of log|sin(logx)| — ∫cott dt integrates to a log of SINE, not cosine.
steps.memory_tip: ∫cott dt = log|sint| (sine); ∫tant dt = −log|cost| (cosine, with a minus) — different results, easy to swap.
